recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. A rename would contradict the work group decision and be a substantive compatibility change, while additional prose would duplicate existing authoritative and narrative scope text without changing implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-20973 asked to rename DocumentReference and redefine its scope for raw binary patient-associated content such as certificates. The final Published / Not Persuasive with Modification decision rejected a rename as too substantive, but asked editors to review whether scope statements could more clearly say the resource is not limited to traditional documents.
initial_application: No current-branch source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-20973. The relevant clarification appears in the source history through earlier and related DocumentReference edits: b7f4a901e1 broadened the introduction after the 2019 Zulip discussion to include clinical notes and other binary objects such as photos, videos, and audio recordings, and the R5 StructureDefinition source later carried the stronger definition that DocumentReference encompasses any serialized object with a mime-type.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread confirms DocumentReference was the intended metadata carrier for raw binary content and that the concern was name/scope clarity. OO minutes from 2022-02-24 record the formal decision not to rename DocumentReference while ensuring the scope is clear. Later Published DocumentReference boundary work, especially FHIR-38950 and FHIR-19250, further reinforces the current narrative that the resource captures data that might not be in FHIR format and is not limited to formal FHIR Documents.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini lists DocumentReference as an active build resource, structuredefinition-DocumentReference.xml already states that the term document encompasses any serialized object with a mime-type, and documentreference-introduction.xml already says DocumentReference indexes other binary objects and that the document can be any object, not limited to formal HL7 FHIR Documents.

related_jiras.note: Later Published DocumentReference boundary clarification that reinforces current wording about non-FHIR objects and DiagnosticReport overlap.
Later Published change, already represented on the combined branch, that added the current narrative that DocumentReference is not limited to formal FHIR Documents.
